label: My HOA won't provide records
summary: Texas does not have a general state agency that regulates property owners' associations. Start with the association's governing documents and Texas Property Code Chapter 209. TREC maintains the statewide HOA management-certificate database but does not regulate HOAs.
primary: Texas Property Code / HOA management-certificate registry
caution: The right remedy depends on the type of association, governing documents, notice history, and the specific records requested.

label: My insurance claim was denied or delayed
summary: The Texas Department of Insurance regulates insurers, agents, adjusters, and other TDI-licensed entities. TDI can help with complaints and explain insurance rules, but private coverage disputes can still require contractual or legal remedies.
caution: A complaint process does not replace policy deadlines, appraisal provisions, suit limitations, or legal advice.

label: I have a problem with an electrician or HVAC contractor
summary: Electricians and air-conditioning/refrigeration contractors are among the occupations licensed by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. Check license status and TDLR enforcement resources before deciding what to do next.
primary: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
caution: Licensing and discipline are separate from recovering money for defective work or a contract dispute.

label: I have a problem with a plumber
summary: Plumbing licenses are handled by the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners. License and complaint procedures are separate from any private claim for damages.
primary: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners
caution: Local permitting and inspection departments can also matter for work performed on a specific property.

label: I have a complaint about a real estate agent or broker
summary: The Texas Real Estate Commission regulates Texas real estate brokers, sales agents, inspectors, and several related license types. TREC has complaint and license-search procedures.
caution: TREC does not generally regulate builders or homeowners associations.

label: I have a complaint about a title company
summary: Title insurance companies and agents are regulated through the Texas Department of Insurance. TREC directs title-company complaints to TDI rather than treating them as real-estate-license complaints.
caution: Escrow, closing, title coverage, and ownership disputes can involve different rules and remedies.

label: My property appraisal is too high
summary: Property appraisal protests begin with your county appraisal district and appraisal review board. The Texas Comptroller publishes statewide guidance, forms, deadlines, and explanations of the protest process.
primary: County appraisal district / Appraisal Review Board
agency: Local appraisal district + Texas Comptroller guidance
caution: Deadlines are strict and can vary based on when notice was delivered and the type of protest.

label: A contractor says they will put a lien on my home
summary: Texas mechanic's-lien rights are governed primarily by Property Code Chapter 53. Filing, notice, homestead, retainage, and deadline rules can differ based on who contracted with whom and the type of project.
primary: Texas Property Code Chapter 53 / county clerk records
caution: Lien validity is fact-specific. The site summarizes public law and cannot determine whether a particular lien is valid.

label: My roofer took a deposit and disappeared
summary: Texas does not use TDLR as a general statewide roofing-contractor licensing authority. Contract, fraud, local permitting, insurance, and court remedies can be more relevant depending on what happened.
primary: Local permitting authority / Texas Attorney General consumer resources / private remedies
agency: No general statewide roofer license through TDLR
caution: Check local permit requirements, written contract terms, payment records, and whether any lien notices have been received.

label: My homebuilder won't fix a defect
summary: TREC states that it does not regulate builders. Builder disputes may involve warranty terms, local building-code enforcement, contracts, statutory consumer protections, arbitration clauses, and private legal remedies.
primary: Contract/warranty + local code authority + applicable Texas law
caution: Construction-defect claims are highly fact-specific and can have notice, inspection, arbitration, and limitations requirements.
